whatItDoes: Shows how many months of expenses your current savings cover and how far you are from a target emergency fund (commonly 3-6 months of expenses). Also shows the target amount you need to reach your chosen coverage.
whyItExists: Emergency savings is the shock absorber between you and debt. Knowing your coverage in months makes the goal concrete and the gap clear, so you can plan how much to save.
whoShouldUse: Anyone building an emergency fund, budgeting households, and people recovering a depleted buffer after an expense.
useCases: See how many months current savings cover
Find the target amount for your goal months
Track progress as the fund grows
Plan a monthly savings goal if you're short
Decide between a 3-month and 6-month buffer based on income stability

instructions: Enter your current emergency fund balance
Read the months covered and target amount

examples: $4,000/month expenses and $20,000 saved → about 5 months covered
$3,500/month expenses and $14,000 saved → exactly 4 months covered — right at the lower end of a healthy range
$5,000/month expenses needing 6 months of coverage → a $30,000 target fund
bestPractices: Use a realistic average of essential monthly expenses
Keep the fund accessible, in a liquid low-risk account
Choose 3-6 months based on income stability
Rebuild the fund after using it via a regular contribution
Revisit the coverage number as expenses change
commonMistakes: Using net-of-discretionary expenses that drift with lifestyle
Keeping the fund in illiquid or volatile investments
Setting a target that doesn't match income stability
Counting investments or retirement accounts that can't be accessed quickly
Basing the fund on aspirational expenses instead of your actual essential outgoings
faq: Does this tool support multiple currencies? — Yes, select your currency from the dropdown. All calculations run locally in your browser.
What is a good emergency fund? — Usually 3-6 months of essential expenses.
Should I also plan other savings? — This covers emergencies only; other goals need separate planning.
Is my data shared? — No, everything runs locally in your browser.
Where should I keep my emergency fund? — A liquid, low-risk account like a high-yield savings account, not volatile investments.
How many months do I need? — 3 months for stable income, closer to 6 months if your income is variable or your expenses are high.
What counts as essential expenses? — Housing, food, utilities, transport, insurance, and minimum debt payments — not discretionary spending.
